focus: Primary navigation and bottom-tab information architecture for ScoreEasy: what the tab bar should hold, tabs vs hub vs profile, label clarity (I-066), and the Home/Play/History/Friends/More question — grounded in the real 60-screen inventory.
navModel: Recommend a 5-slot bottom tab bar with Play as an emphasized center action: Home · History · [Play] · Watch/Friends · Profile. Rationale: (1) This is a mobile-first phone app (300x600 HiFi frames, device-chrome fidelity) — a persistent bottom tab bar is the correct primary model, and the current 3-tab bar (Play/History/Stats) under-uses it. (2) 'Start & score a match' is the app's core job, so Play belongs in the center as a raised/emphasized CTA rather than a peer tab — it is the one action every session funnels through. (3) Home must become a real tab: today Dashboard (landing/DashboardLanding.jsx) exists but is NOT in the tab bar, so signed-in users have no persistent 'home' anchor for the live/upcoming feed HiFi wants. (4) Stats should NOT hold a scarce tab slot — it is low-frequency and empty for new users (I-013); fold it under History or Profile. (5) The 4th slot is the growth axis: today it should hold Profile/account (avatar target promoted to a tab), and as the social layer lands it becomes Watch/Friends with Profile moving behind the avatar or into a More sheet. PHASING: ship now as Home · History · [Play] · Profile (4 real destinations that exist); add the Watch/Friends tab only once Activity feed + spectator ship, so you never show a tab that opens an empty shell. Everything account/settings/teams/notifications hangs off Profile as a hub (profile-as-hub) rather than eating tab slots — HiFi's 'More/Settings' is a Profile sub-surface, not a 5th tab, until social forces the split.
discoverabilityIssues: No Home tab: DashboardLanding.jsx (the signed-in home) is reachable via /dashboard redirect but absent from the tab bar (index.jsx:566-582 = Play/History/Stats only), so users have no persistent anchor to return to.
Profile is not a tab: /profile is reachable only by tapping the avatar — account, and therefore any future settings/friends/teams that hang off it, are one undiscoverable tap deep with no label.
User search (/users/search, MonoUserSearch.jsx) has NO entry point in the primary nav — the closest thing to 'find friends' is effectively orphaned.
Settings has no route at all — scoring defaults, dark mode, auto-share, data export/clear (all in HiFi's More·settings) have nowhere to live and nowhere to be discovered.
Watch-live / spectator has no nav home — even setting aside the missing feature, there is no tab or entry where a 'friends are live now' feed would surface.
Tournament entry is buried inside the per-sport Play flow (:sport/tournament) — there is no top-level path to competitions; a user in History or Home cannot reach fixtures/standings.
Stats occupies a top-level tab but for a new user it renders empty (I-013), so a prime tab slot leads to a dead-end on first run.
Notifications (friend requests, live alerts, milestones) have no bell/entry anywhere.

HOME becomes the real signed-in dashboard carrying a Live-now strip + Start CTA + activity feed (today Play doubles as home, and /, /dashboard, /play triple up on "home"). focus: Simplicity, cognitive load, and first-run clarity — how ScoreEasy's IA overwhelms, where the next action is unclear, and where progressive disclosure/defaults/empty-state guidance are missing.
navModel: Adopt the HiFi 4-tab bottom nav — Home · Play · History · More — with Home as the signed-in default, not Play. Rationale: today the app shell has only 3 tabs (Play / History / Stats, index.jsx:566-582) and lands signed-in users straight into a "pick a sport" chore with no orientation. A Home tab (live/upcoming feed + recent activity + one primary "Start a match" CTA) gives a low-cognitive-load entry that answers "what now?" in one glance, and absorbs the thin /dashboard. Play stays the single funnel into match creation. History subsumes Stats/leaderboard/profile behind one tab (they are all "the record"), fixing the Stats-vs-Statistics split. More becomes the home for Settings, Profile/account, Friends, Teams — all the low-frequency surfaces that currently have no shelf. Keep it 4 tabs max; do NOT add Friends as a 5th top-level tab until the social layer actually exists — nest it under More/Home-feed first.
discoverabilityIssues: Signed-in users land on Play (pick-a-sport) with no Home/orientation surface — Dashboard exists (landing/DashboardLanding.jsx) but is thin and not the tab default; the HiFi live/upcoming/Activity feed is absent, so there is no 'what's happening' entry point.

No Settings route exists at all — scoring defaults, the 'Confirm wicket/goal' toggle, auto-share, dark mode (declared-but-unused .dark in index.css), and data export are undiscoverable because they have nowhere to live; Profile (MonoProfile 394ln) is the only account surface.

Match-end is a dead end: no Result/Scorecard/Share-card screen ships, so after the final point the scorer has no designed terminal state and no obvious next action (Done/Rematch/Share are undiscoverable).
Share-live / spectator / QR only exist in a worktree branch, not production — the entire 'let someone watch' capability is invisible to real users.

Two cricket start paths (I-085: :sport/quick/test-match vs dispatched limited-overs inside MonoQuickMatch 2850ln) mean the same intent forks unpredictably — the user can't tell which door leads where.
Customize & rules is embedded/implicit inside MonoQuickMatch rather than a labeled step, so rule customization is hidden behind the setup monolith.
Statistics depth (charts/trends/head-to-head/leaderboard) is buried inside one table-heavy /statistics screen with no visualization layer anywhere in the app.
simplicityRecommendations: Design the three empty/first-run states HiFi calls for (Home-empty, History-empty, Teams-empty) — today the app renders zero-grids or risks perpetual loading (I-053). Each empty state should carry ONE primary CTA ('Start your first match') so first-run has an obvious next action instead of a blank grid.
Simplify onboarding to the HiFi shape: Continue with Google / Apple / phone → Home. MonoOnboarding.jsx is 922ln — heavy for a first impression; strip it to auth + land on the empty Home.

Collapse the Play → Sport home → Quick match layering. There are two 'pick' layers (MonoPlayHub then MonoSportHome) plus a 2850ln setup monolith. Make Play one screen: pick sport → clean Setup → (optional Customize & rules) → scorer. Split MonoQuickMatch so Setup/Toss/Customize are distinct, minimal screens.

Use defaults + progressive disclosure to reduce choices: default sport (from Settings) so returning users skip the sport picker; make 'Confirm wicket/goal' a settings toggle (not an always-on interrupt); keep rare inputs behind long-press (Cricket long-press No-ball→runs) so the primary scorer stays clean.
Make attribution optional-by-default: every who-scored/how-out/credit-point sheet must have a prominent Skip alongside Confirm so casual scorers are never forced through stat entry.
Add the team-only (no-roster) casual mode HiFi Band 8 specifies — the fastest path to 'just keep score' with zero player-setup cognitive load.

Do NOT expose the refined/new/old scorer-style toggle to end users — it is a design-exploration mechanism; shipping three co-located scorer variants would multiply choice and overwhelm. Pick 'refined' and hide the rest.
Fix history's mobile overload (I-086): the 3-col summary + search/filter block consumes the viewport before any result. Demote filters behind a collapsed control and lead with results.
Reduce top-level tabs to 4 and push low-frequency surfaces (Settings, Teams, Friends, account Profile) under More, so the primary surface stays glanceable.
